drafts.walkScript: Line 21 says the party "entered" the room and "consisted of only five". Line 22 lists the five: Mr Bingley and the people who came with him. So a party here is a group of people who arrive together. It is not everyone at the assembly, and it is not the ball.

Read lines 29 and 30 and find the words "growing out of the top". Something growing out of the top of a wall is a plant. Line 30 adds "the window-shape" as a second, separate thing. So the elder is the growing one, a small tree or bush. An older member of a family cannot grow out of a wall.

Line 45 says "being useful, or at least officious", so officious falls short of truly useful. Lines 40 and 41 show Jane "would not be driven quite away" when told to move. So officious means being useful in a pushy way, going further than is wanted. She "drew near him again" on lines 45 and 46, but officious does not mean that. The word has nothing to do with holding an office.
Read on from line 8, past the shouting. Lines 8 and 9 say he goes "without even waiting to put on his coat". So he rushed out suddenly. Locking and eating are the other senses.
